## Big idea

Some needs touch many methods: logging, timing, transactions, security.  
Copy-paste into every method is bad. **AOP** adds that behavior around methods using **proxies**.

```text
Caller → Spring proxy → @Before advice → real method → @After advice → back
```

## Terms

| Term | Plain meaning |
|------|----------------|
| Cross-cutting concern | Logic needed in many places |
| Advice | The extra code (before/after/around) |
| Pointcut | Which methods get the advice |
| Proxy | Wrapper object Spring injects instead of the raw bean |

## Practice mindset

Call a `@Service` method from another bean (not `this` inside same class) so the proxy applies.
